Re: Petition for Public Records Disclosure Order:
State Board of Psychologist Examiners Records
Dear Mr. Eccles:
JACK L. LANDAU
DEPUTY ATIORNEY GENERAL
This letter is the Attorney General's order on your petition for disclosure of
records under the Oregon Public Records Law, ORS 192.410 to 192.505. Your petition,
which we received on April9, 1992, asks the Attorney General to direct the State Board
of Psychologist Examiners (board) to provide you with copies of board notices of various
of its meetings "that [are] printed on something other than the Board of Psychologist
Examiners stationery, that is, newspaper, etc." For the reasons that follow, we
respectfully deny your petition.
The board has informed us that the meeting notices that you received are the only
notices it prepares and distributes to news media and interested persons. Public bodies
are not required by the Oregon Public Meetings Law to publish their meeting notices in
newspapers. See ORS 192.640(1). Because the board has no records that satisfy your
request, there is no basis upon which the Attorney General can order the board to
disclose such records.
On page two of your petition, you petition for disclosure· of the names and
addresses of the local news media, organizations and individuals who receive the board's
meeting notices. The board has informed us that it has not received a request from you
for such records. Absent a request to the board and a denial by the board, the Attorney
James R. Eccles

General does not have jurisdiction to order disclosure. ORS 192.450. Because the board
has not denied your requests, your petition with respect to these records is premature and
is, therefore, denied.
